site.title: Boot. Fix. Test. Fully Automatic.
site.description: Knecht is a dashboard on your own server for agencies with many DDEV projects. It boots each project as an operational environment, does tasks in workflows, and supplies completed pull requests with a preview.

hero.title: Boot. Fix. Test.
hero.description: Knecht is a dashboard on your server, made for agencies with many DDEV projects. A GitHub issue or Jira ticket starts a workflow. Knecht boots the project as a working environment, does the task from the ticket there, and supplies a completed pull request with a preview.
hero.mascotAlt: Knecht, the robot helper with a CRT screen head

integrations.title: Knecht Connects to the Tools You Already Use.
integrations.intro: A ticket comes in, a result goes out. In between, Knecht boots your project and works in the real system.

github.title: GitHub
github.text: Starts a workflow from an issue, a label, or a mention.

jira.title: Jira
jira.text: Starts a workflow from a ticket or a label and comments back.

cron.title: Cron & Webhook
cron.text: Runs on a schedule or when a security advisory comes in.

center.text: A complete environment with web, database, and services.

pr.title: Pull Request

useCases.title: Three Examples from
useCases.intro: Knecht does every task that you can describe as a workflow. These three show what such a run looks like, from the trigger to the pull request.

security.title: A Security Update with the Database Running.
security.text: A patch for your CMS comes out. Knecht boots each affected project with its database, installs the update, runs the migrations, and commits everything that comes out of it.
security.before: Dependabot opens a PR without the migration files. Someone has to boot locally, migrate, and commit again.
security.after: Update, migrations, and preview in one run. The PR is complete when it opens.

estimate.title: Estimate a Ticket Before Anyone Spends Time on It.
estimate.text: A new Jira ticket gets the label "knecht-estimate". Knecht reads the code in the live project, finds the cause, and writes effort, risk, and a suggested fix as a comment in the ticket.
estimate.before: The ticket waits for the next planning. The estimate is a gut feeling.
estimate.after: An assessment in minutes, based on the real code, directly as a comment in the ticket.

analyze.label: Analysis
analyze.title: Knecht reads code & reproduces
analyze.detail: Form handler, queue, and 2 templates affected

assess.label: Assessment
assess.title: Effort & risk
assess.detail: About 3 hours, low risk, one module

result.label: Result
result.title: Comment in the ticket
result.detail: Assessment, suggestion, and the offer to fix it

out.head: Comment in KAN-231
out.body: Cause: duplicate event listener in newsletter.js. Effort ≈ 3 h, low risk. Suggestion: centralize the listener in init(). Should I prepare the fix as a PR?

fix.title: Fix the Bug from the Issue, Tested Against the Real App.
fix.text: An issue gets the label "knecht-fix". Knecht boots the project, reproduces the bug in the preview, fixes it, and opens a pull request with a preview link you can click through.
fix.before: A coding agent guesses blindly whether the fix works. You have to test it yourself.
fix.after: The agent sees the live app, reproduces the bug, and tests the fix against it.

techStack.title: Tech Stack and Architecture

dashboardDesign.text: The design for the dashboard is complete. In the dashboard, you make projects and workflows.

installer.title: Installer
installer.text: You can install the dashboard on each Linux server.

updateService.title: Update Service
updateService.text: You can install updates from the control panel.

githubTrigger.title: GitHub Trigger
githubTrigger.text: You can set GitHub triggers that start workflows.

knechtLives.title: Knecht Is Alive
knechtLives.text: You can install the Knecht dashboard on a Linux server with low effort, and it gets updates.

sshIde.title: SSH and IDE
sshIde.text: You can make changes in the live preview containers through SSH and an IDE.

feedbackLoop.title: Feedback Loop
feedbackLoop.text: After a workflow run, different feedback functions are necessary to make the output better.

managedHosting.title: Managed Hosting
managedHosting.text: Beta testers do not have to install Knecht themselves. We host the instance for them and take care of updates and operations.

langdockSupport.title: Langdock Support
langdockSupport.text: The agent also runs through Langdock. One API key covers GPT and Claude models, and every request stays in the EU.

agentHistory.title: Agent History
agentHistory.text: Every issue gets its own session. The agent keeps its environment and conversation across multiple runs.

betaTesters.title: Find Beta Testers
betaTesters.text: We look for a sufficient number of beta testers to find problems early and build the final product.

testActions.title: Test Actions
testActions.text: Workflows can run tests for projects. A fix is complete only when the tests are green.

browserValidation.title: Browser Validation
browserValidation.text: The agent examines the bug in the preview and supplies screenshots as proof.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.text: Slack or email sends a message when a run is complete or when it fails.

docs.title: Documentation and Onboarding
